summary: This informational document defines and registers the value "impp" (instant messaging and presence protocol) for the "purpose" parameter of the SIP Call-Info header field.

eli5.summary: A call can carry a note pointing to chat and online-status details. This adds the label for that kind of note.

subtitle: Registering 'impp' for advertising instant messaging addresses in SIP calls.

tldr.problem: Endpoints that support both SIP (for voice/video calls) and XMPP (for instant messaging and presence) needed a way to advertise their instant messaging addresses to SIP users, to improve interoperability.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6993 registers the value 'impp' (instant messaging and presence protocol) for the 'purpose' parameter of the SIP Call-Info header field, allowing endpoints to include instant messaging contact information.
tldr.outcome: SIP users can now discover instant messaging addresses of endpoints during SIP communication, enabling seamless switching between voice calls and instant messaging.

today: RFC 6993 is an Informational RFC that registered the 'impp' value for SIP Call-Info headers. It enables endpoints supporting both SIP and instant messaging protocols to advertise their instant messaging addresses during SIP communication.

sections.title: Bridging Voice Calls and Instant Messaging
sections.content:
Some modern communication endpoints support two different protocols at the same time:

SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) is used for voice calls, video calls, and real-time communication. XMPP (Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol) is used for instant messaging and presence information (like whether someone is online or away). These endpoints are called CUSAX endpoints—Combined Use of SIP And XMPP.

To help these endpoints work together better, they need to advertise both their SIP addresses and their XMPP addresses. RFC 6993 enables advertising an instant messaging address during a SIP call using the Call-Info header field, which carries additional information about a call.

The example from the RFC shows what this looks like: Call-Info: <xmpp:juliet@example.com> ;purpose=impp. This tells the receiving endpoint that the caller also has an instant messaging address at juliet@example.com on XMPP.
sections.eli5: When you call someone over SIP, you can also leave a note saying where to find them on instant messaging. It makes it easy to switch from a call to a chat.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Advertising an instant messaging address carries some risks. A malicious person could spoof the Call-Info header and claim a false instant messaging address. Endpoints receiving this header should check it against a trusted source like a user directory to verify it is authentic.

The header field can be protected using encryption (S/MIME for end-to-end protection, or TLS for hop-by-hop protection) to ensure it cannot be modified in transit.

Privacy is also a concern: connecting a SIP address to an XMPP address creates a correlation between two different communication identities that might otherwise be unconnected. User agents should let users control whether this information is sent to others.
sections.eli5: Someone could fake this note, so you should check it is real. It also connects two identities, which might reveal information a user wants private.

sections.title: Registration
sections.content: RFC 6993 defines and registers 'impp' as a predefined value for the 'purpose' parameter of the Call-Info header field. This registration with IANA makes it an official part of the SIP protocol registry, allowing all endpoints to recognize and use this value consistently.
sections.eli5: The registration made 'impp' official, so now all SIP endpoints can use it the same way.
